title: Function-free optimization via comparison oracles
contribution: A function-free framework for optimising a preference relation from pairwise comparisons alone: level-set optimality gap and regularity radius as invariant measures, a deterministic O(d log(d/eps)) normal-direction estimator matching an Omega(d log(1/eps)) lower bound, and NDD/adaNDD reaching an eps level-set gap with O~(dD^2/eps^2) comparisons over O(D^2/eps^2) normal steps, matching a span-method lower bound.
problem_entry: Modelling objection: prior comparison-oracle work treats comparisons as a weak interface to a latent objective and states guarantees in function terms, yet preference-equivalent functions (Figure 1) give identical trajectories, so guarantees must depend only on the preference relation (pp. 2-3, 10-11).
key_idea: Replace gradient, f-f* and stationarity by the outward normal of the preference sublevel set, dist(X*, L_x) and the tangent-ball regularity radius; estimate the normal via its orthogonal complement with d-1 planar bisections; run normalized-gradient descent / KT coin-betting on the estimated normals (pp. 3-4, 14-16, 28-36).
assumptions: Complete, transitive, plateau-free preference; convex sublevel sets for global results; r-regularity (two-sided tangent balls); noiseless comparison oracle; projections onto C; local growth r_x >= min{g1*Delta_LS, g2} to convert stationarity to optimality (pp. 7-9, 11, 32).
proof_devices: halfspace certificate with margin tau = h/(2 r_x) from tangent-ball geometry (Lemma 3.1)
planar bisection bracket invariant (Lemma 3.3)
orthonormal decomposition separating geometry bias from bisection error (Thm 3.5)
Haar anti-concentration plus randomly rotated dyadic grid for a high-probability halving count (Lemmas 3.8-3.9, Thm 3.11)
adversarial halving of spherical cells plus cap volume and Wendel's inequality for Omega(d log(1/eps)) (Thm 3.14)
supporting-halfspace bound Delta_LS(x) <= <n_x, x - x*> and monotonicity of Delta_LS (Lemmas 4.2-4.3)
Shor normalized-subgradient telescoping with accumulated estimation error, two-case guarantee (Thm 4.4)
KT coin-betting regret with projection-correction inequality and budget-exhaustion certificate via union bound (Lemmas 4.15-4.18, Thm 4.19)
zero-chain max_i x_i instance smoothed by convolution with an ordered-simplex kernel (Thm 4.23)
positioning: Reframes rather than attacks comparison-based DFO (Hooke-Jeeves, Nelder-Mead, three-point, GLD, Jamieson et al., dueling optimization); translates competing normalized-gradient estimators into its notation and compares admissible comparison radius and count; acknowledges concurrent Tao et al.; cites no Scheinberg paper (pp. 2, 5-6, 17-18, 26, 44-46).
writing: Three numbered Questions mapped to sections and contributions; one motivating figure; two named principles (optimality, adaptivity); interpretation paragraph after each theorem ('price of adaptivity'); rare flagged hedging; minor typos (pp. 2-4, 17, 23, 32, 44).
limits_future: Global guarantees need convexity; noiseless oracle; lower bounds only for direction estimation and span-method step count, the minimax comparison complexity is open; nonconvex function-free theory open; no experiments (pp. 8, 11, 44).

quotes.text: In summary, prior work aims to optimize a scalar function through weaker oracles. In contrast, our central goal is to formulate an optimization problem when the preference relation itself is the basic object defining optimality.
Optimality matters because we seek worst-case complexity guarantees that cannot be substantially improved in general.

title: First-and Second-Order Stochastic Adaptive Regularization with Cubics: High-Probability Iteration and Sample Complexity
contribution: First high-probability (and expected) iteration complexity O(eps^-3/2) for first- and second-order stochastic ARC under stochastic zeroth-, first- and second-order oracles, matching deterministic ARC, plus high-probability sample complexity O(eps^-3.5) gradient, O(eps^-2.5) Hessian and O(eps^-4.5) function samples, with a noise floor O(eps_f^(2/3)).
problem_entry: ARC is the deterministic winner (eps^-3/2 vs eps^-2), but stochastic ARC analyses give only expected bounds with exact or bounded zeroth-order oracles, or are non-adaptive with bounds holding only on an accuracy event (TSJ+18) (p. 2).
key_idea: Keep ARC; tie oracle accuracy inputs to the regularisation parameter (mu/sigma_k for gradients, sqrt(mu/sigma_k) for Hessians), add a 2eps'_f slack to the acceptance ratio, and read alpha_k = 1/sigma_k as a step parameter so the JSX24 process framework applies (pp. 4, 10-11).
assumptions: C^2, L-Lipschitz gradient and L_H-Lipschitz Hessian, bounded below; SZO sub-exponential error with mean <= eps_f; SFO/SSO accurate to kappa*mu w.p. 1-delta, implementable for arbitrarily small mu (stronger than JSX24/CBS22); p > 1/2; unbiased bounded-variance minibatches for sample complexity (pp. 1-3, 9, 16).
proof_devices: per-realisation lemmas: model decrease sigma|s|^3/6, large sigma => success or tiny step, step-norm lower bound via gradient at trial point (Lemmas 1-5)
hypothesis-checklist theorem verifying JSX24 properties (i)-(v) with one-line glosses (Theorem 2)
imported JSX24 tail bound with stopping time shifted to T_eps <= t+1 (Theorem 3)
Borel-Cantelli for a.s. finite stopping time and expectation from exponential tail (Remark 3)
second-order step lower bound via Hessian Lipschitz, SSO accuracy and relaxed Nesterov-Polyak condition (Lemma 9)
one-sided geometric random walk bound on sigma_k via JSX25 Theorem 3 plus Chebyshev minibatch sizes for sample complexity (Theorems 6-7)
experiments: none (explicitly: numerical performance not discussed because ARC efficiency depends on the subproblem solver, p. 3)
positioning: Extends JSX24 and CBS22 to the CS18 framework; presents SZO/SFO/SSO as a shared standard across group and others' papers; concrete critique of TSJ+18 and an even-handed sample-complexity comparison with it (pp. 2-3, 19).
writing: Abstract claims SARC outperforms other stochastic adaptive methods from complexity alone; 'first comprehensive analysis' contributions; stronger assumption disclosed upfront with a why-it-rarely-binds argument; roadmap paragraph before lemmas; glosses on theorem items (pp. 1, 3, 5, 10).
limits_future: Stronger SFO/SSO assumption; relaxed step-dependent oracle inputs left open; no numerics; dimension ignored in sample counts; function-sample complexity worse than methods without function values (pp. 3, 5, 16, 19).

title: Powell-Style Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization with Complexity Guarantees
contribution: Complexity O(n^{3/2} log n eps^-2) function evaluations for a Powell-style geometry-correcting trust-region method that keeps all sample points and fits quadratic models, noisy random-subspace bounds O(nq/eps^2) and O(nq log q/eps^2), and a practical GC-YZ-LIN implementation with a hedge model that matches NEWUOA on CUTEst.
problem_entry: Practice-theory gap: Powell's methods (revived in PDFO/PRIMA) work well but existing complexity covers simplified methods that rebuild models and abandon Powell's geometry handling; even [11] discards useful points; since all methods are O(eps^-2), target the n-dependence and noise floor (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Split samples into a certified core Y (n points, linear Lagrange polynomials, Lambda-poised) and a reuse pool Z fitted by least squares; replace the criticality step by ||g_k|| >= eta2*Delta_k with eta2 = sqrt(n); count geometry steps with a determinant potential; in noisy subspaces add +2eps_f and an explicit Delta_min (pp. 4, 7, 10-18).
assumptions: Bounded below, L-Lipschitz gradient; deterministic bounded noise |f - phi| <= eps_f; fraction of Cauchy decrease and bounded model Hessian; subspace alignment w.p. theta > 1/2 (243/443 for uniform subspaces); Assumption 6.1 for practical gates; theory for linear Lagrange polynomials only (pp. 2, 4, 20, 24).
proof_devices: TR counting: small Delta + fully linear => success, success => C2 Delta^2 - 2eps_f decrease, radius lower bound, |U| <= |S| + log (Lemmas 2.3-2.7, Thm 2.8)
explicit n-tracking of constants C1, C2 giving the eta2 = sqrt(n) gain (Cor. 2.10)
Lambda-poised error bound with quadratic term and noise via linearity of Lagrange polynomials (Thms 3.3, 3.5)
-log|det Y| potential: Hadamard, Cramer's rule, AM-GM on singular values give (1-1/n) contraction (Lemma 4.2)
induction on subspace dimension for 14^n-poisedness after 2n steps (Lemma 4.3)
indicator processes I_t, A_t, B_t with A_t >= I_t(1-B_t) and Cartis-Scheinberg renewal lemmas for E[T_eps] <= 4theta/(2theta-1)^2 (...) (Thm 5.12)
experiments: CUTEst via S2MPJ: 174 problems with n in [2,5] and 95/101/92 problems at n = 30/100/200; GC-YZ-LIN, GC-YZ-V, NEWUOA (PRIMA), DFOTR, GC-sub (q = 5); data profiles at tau in {1e-2,1e-4,1e-6} with AUC, averaged over random rotations of initial sets; hedge model given to all solvers; negative subspace result reported (pp. 26-30).
positioning: Sequel to [11] (Chaudhry-Scheinberg, ICM 2026) with an error corrected in a footnote; criticises Garmanjani-Judice-Vicente's simplified methods; credits Zhang's PDFO/PRIMA; comparative subspace lineage (GRVZ18, Cartis-Roberts, Dzahini-Wild); sends readers to Cartis-Roberts for subspace experiments (pp. 1-2, 5, 10, 16, 30).
writing: Abstract hedges 'what we believe to be nearly tight'; bullet recap of [11] and bullet list of extensions; 'Let us pause' constants paragraph; 'We state upfront' numbered findings incl. negative; admits surprise; scopes down subspace contribution; some drafting inconsistencies (pp. 1-2, 6-7, 12, 26, 29-30).
limits_future: Theory for linear Lagrange polynomials only (best performer GC-YZ-V uncovered); practical subspace not competitive; practical parameters far from theory; subspace restarts expensive; future: quadratic Lagrange theory, adaptive eta2 and Lambda, patience theory, small subspace sets and point reuse (pp. 22, 24-25, 27, 29-30).
